cases.title: SQBench: Lacto-fermentation diary
cases.semantic_query: How do I keep mold from growing when lacto-fermenting cabbage at home in a jar?
cases.body:
# Diary

tok_sqbench_e4f9201

A two to three percent salt brine by weight keeps lacto-fermentation anaerobic enough that spoilage bacteria stay suppressed. Keep vegetables fully submerged under a weight and burp the jar daily for the first week. Room temperature around eighteen to twenty-two Celsius works well for sauerkraut.

cases.title: SQBench: Tree rotations
cases.semantic_query: When does a binary search tree need a left-right double rotation after an insert?
cases.body:
# Notes

tok_sqbench_e4f9202

A double rotation fixes the AVL imbalance pattern where the child subtree grows heavy on the outside opposite side. After inserting into the left subtree of a right-heavy node’s right child, you rotate the child first then the parent. This restores the height balance invariant while keeping the BST ordering property.

## History

tok_sqbench_e4f9203

The Althing met at Thingvellir, a rift valley where lawspeakers recited the law code each summer. Free farmers gathered to hear judgments and settle feuds before the Norwegian crown tightened control. The site symbolised communal governance long before a national parliament building existed.

cases.title: SQBench: Sourdough basics
cases.semantic_query: Why do bakers rest flour and water before adding salt to sourdough?
cases.body:
# Baking

tok_sqbench_e4f9204

Autolyse lets flour fully hydrate and gluten begin developing without salt tightening the dough. After thirty to sixty minutes the dough feels smoother and extensible. Salt is folded in afterward so fermentation timing stays predictable.

cases.title: SQBench: TCP congestion
cases.semantic_query: What happens to the congestion window at the start of a new TCP connection?
cases.body:
# Networking

tok_sqbench_e4f9205

Slow start grows the congestion window exponentially while acknowledgements arrive on time. Packet loss triggers multiplicative decrease and often switches the sender into congestion avoidance. The goal is to probe available bandwidth without collapsing router queues.

cases.title: SQBench: Nutrition note

cases.body:
## Diet

tok_sqbench_e4f9206

Vitamin B12 is synthesised by bacteria, not by plants, so strict vegans rely on fortified foods or supplements. Nutritional yeast and plant milks are common fortified sources. Blood tests help catch deficiency before nerve damage appears.

cases.title: SQBench: Go Dockerfile multi-stage image shrink
cases.semantic_query: How does a multi-stage Dockerfile reduce final image size for a Go service?
cases.body:
# DevOps

tok_sqbench_e4f9207

For a **Go service**, a **multi-stage Dockerfile** first uses a fat `golang` image to `go build -ldflags="-w -s"` a static Linux binary, then copies only that binary into a tiny runtime such as `scratch` or `distroless/static`. The **final image** drops compilers, module caches, and source trees, so **image size** shrinks from gigabytes to tens of megabytes. Each `FROM` begins a new stage; only `COPY --from=builder` artifacts cross the boundary.

cases.title: SQBench: OAuth2 PKCE for mobile authorization code
cases.semantic_query: Why is PKCE recommended for OAuth2 authorization code flows in public mobile apps?
cases.body:
# Security

tok_sqbench_e4f9209

**PKCE** (RFC 7636) extends the **OAuth2 authorization code** grant for **public mobile apps** that cannot hide a client secret. The app sends a `code_challenge` with the authorize URL and later proves it holds the matching `code_verifier` at the **token endpoint**, so a stolen redirect **authorization code** alone is useless. Native iOS and Android OAuth guides therefore mandate **PKCE** for any **public** client using the code flow.

cases.title: SQBench: PostgreSQL partial index vs full table index
cases.semantic_query: When is a partial PostgreSQL index better than indexing the whole table?
cases.body:
# SQL

tok_sqbench_e4f9211

In **PostgreSQL**, a **partial index** is declared with `CREATE INDEX ... WHERE <predicate>` so only rows satisfying that predicate enter the btree. That beats **indexing the whole table** when the hot queries always filter the same way—for example `WHERE archived = false` on a mostly-historical ledger. The planner can pick the partial index only when the query `WHERE` clause implies the same condition, keeping writes and vacuum work smaller than a monolithic index on every row.

cases.title: SQBench: Crypto engineering
cases.semantic_query: Why choose OAEP padding instead of PKCS1 v1.5 for RSA encryption of a session key?
cases.body:
## Crypto

tok_sqbench_e4f9214

OAEP adds a randomised Feistel mask so ciphertexts are semantically secure under chosen plaintext models. PKCS1 v1.5 padding has been fragile in implementations against bleichenbacher-style attacks. Modern protocols default to OAEP for small payloads.

cases.title: SQBench: CRDT map last-writer-wins concurrent keys
cases.semantic_query: How does last-writer-wins resolve concurrent edits in a CRDT map?
cases.body:
# Systems

tok_sqbench_e4f9219

A replicated **CRDT map** stores per-key registers. Under **last-writer-wins**, each **concurrent edit** to the same key ships a `(timestamp, replica_id)` tuple; replicas merge by keeping the value whose tuple sorts highest, discarding the loser. This gives deterministic convergence without locking, at the cost of dropping causally concurrent updates users might have wanted to merge manually.
